opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Donna Ball (E024) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is limited to the role that owns the system (Engineer for Source Code), so write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Donna Ball (E024) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors with basic training may have at most read; write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two agent notes conflict: HR reports Donna Ball (E024) as full-time (max write, so write would be allowed), while Security reports she is a contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training, so requested write exceeds max and should be read). Given the direct contradiction on employment type and the policy's restrictive treatment of contractors, I grant the safer, policy-compliant level: read.

- Note 2 (Security?): says employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Donna Ball is a Payroll Specialist (per HR note). So even if full-time, admin would not be allowed since Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code. But write is allowed for full-time.

If contractor with basic training, max is read.
